###############################################################################
## Copyright (C) 2023-2026 Analog Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
### SPDX short identifier: ADIBSD
###############################################################################

###############################################################################
# This file contains the following procedures for Lattice Radiant projects:
# * adi_project - Sets the device settings based on project_name or manually
#     by options.
#               - Calls the adi_project_create procedure
#               - Optionally you can add a list of tcl commands to be executed
#     in adi_project_create after creating the project.
# * adi_project_create - Creates the Radiant project itself and executes some
#     optional commands that are piped trough adi_project procedure.
# * adi_project_files_auto - Adds files to the project automatically.
# * adi_project_files - Adds a manually defined list of files to the project.
# * get_file_list - Searches for files or file extensions in a specified
#     directory, returns a list of file paths.
# * adopt_path - No use case yet.
# * adi_project_run - Runs the Radiant project with specified option.
#                   - Optionally runs a list of tcl commands before running the
#     project.
# * adi_project_run_cmd - Opens the Radinat project and runs a list of tcl
#     commands given as parameter.
###############################################################################

###############################################################################
## Extracts the device parameters from project name.
## Calls the adi_project_create procedure with specified parameters.
## There is option to pass the Device parameters manually, and an options
## to pass a list of tcl commands to be executed after creating the project in
## adi_project_create procedure.
#
# \opt[dev_select] -dev_select "auto"
# \opt[ppath] -ppath ./
# \opt[device] -device "LFCPNX-100-9LFG672C"
# \opt[speed] -speed "9_High-Performance_1.0V"
# \opt[board] -board "Certus Pro NX Evaluation Board"
# \opt[synthesis] -synthesis "synplify"
# \opt[impl] -impl "impl_1"
# \opt[cmd_list] -cmd_list {{source ./csacsi.tcl} {source ./a_szamar.tcl}}
###############################################################################
proc adi_project {project_name args} {
  puts "\nadi_project:\n"

  array set opt [list -dev_select "auto" \
    -ppath "./_bld/$project_name" \
    -device "" \
    -speed "" \
    -board "" \
    -synthesis "synplify" \
    -impl "impl_1" \
    -cmd_list "" {*}$args]

  set dev_select $opt(-dev_select)
  set ppath $opt(-ppath)
  set synthesis $opt(-synthesis)
  set impl $opt(-impl)
  set cmd_list $opt(-cmd_list)

  global ad_hdl_dir

  if { [string match "auto" $dev_select] } {
    source $ad_hdl_dir/projects/scripts/adi_lattice_dev_select.tcl
  } elseif { [string match "manual" $dev_select] } {
    set device $opt(-device)
    set board $opt(-board)
    set speed $opt(-speed)
  }

  adi_project_create $project_name \
    -ppath $ppath \
    -device $device \
    -performance $speed \
    -board $board \
    -synthesis $synthesis \
    -impl $impl \
    -cmd_list $cmd_list
}

###############################################################################
## Creates a Radiant project with specified parameters.
## There is an option to run a list of tcl commands given as parameter after
## creating the Radiant design.
#
# \opt[ppath] -ppath ./
# \opt[device] -device "LFCPNX-100-9LFG672C"
# \opt[performance] -performance "9_High-Performance_1.0V"
# \opt[board] -board "Certus Pro NX Evaluation Board"
# \opt[synthesis] -synthesis "synplify"
# \opt[impl] -impl "impl_1"
# \opt[cmd_list] -cmd_list {{source ./csacsi.tcl} {source ./a_szamar.tcl}}
###############################################################################
proc adi_project_create {project_name args}  {
  puts "\nadi_project_create:\n"

  array set opt [list -ppath "./_bld/$project_name" \
    -device "" \
    -performance "" \
    -board "" \
    -synthesis "synplify" \
    -impl "impl_1" \
    -cmd_list "" {*}$args]

  set ppath $opt(-ppath)
  set device $opt(-device)
  set performance $opt(-performance)
  set board $opt(-board)
  set synthesis $opt(-synthesis)
  set impl $opt(-impl)
  set cmd_list $opt(-cmd_list)

  global ad_hdl_dir
  global ad_ghdl_dir
  global ad_project_dir
  global required_lattice_version
  global IGNORE_VERSION_CHECK
  global env

  puts "\nProject name:   $project_name"
  puts "Device:   $device"
  puts "Performance:  $performance"
  puts "Board:  $board\n"

  ## Extracting the Radiant version using sys_install_version command from
  ## propel builder.
  set RADIANT_VERSION [string range [sys_install_version] 0 \
    [expr {[string first "." [sys_install_version]] + 1}]]
  puts "Radiant version: $RADIANT_VERSION\n"

  if {$IGNORE_VERSION_CHECK} {
    if {[string compare $RADIANT_VERSION $required_lattice_version] != 0} {
      puts -nonewline "CRITICAL WARNING: Radiant version mismatch; "
      puts -nonewline "expected $required_lattice_version, "
      puts -nonewline "got $RADIANT_VERSION.\n"
    }
  } else {
    if {[string compare $RADIANT_VERSION $required_lattice_version] != 0} {
      puts -nonewline "ERROR: Radiant version mismatch; "
      puts -nonewline "expected $required_lattice_version, "
      puts -nonewline "got $RADIANT_VERSION.\n"
      puts -nonewline "This ERROR message can be down-graded to CRITICAL \
        WARNING by setting ADI_IGNORE_VERSION_CHECK environment variable to 1. \
        Be aware that ADI will not support you, if you are using a different \
        tool version.\n"
      exit 2
    }
  }

  set dir [pwd]

  if {[file exists $ppath] != 1} {
    file mkdir $ppath
  }
  cd $ppath

  if { [file exists $project_name.rdf] == 1} {
    prj_open $project_name.rdf
    prj_set_device -part $device -performance $performance
  } else {
    prj_create -name "$project_name" \
      -impl $impl \
      -dev $device \
      -performance $performance \
      -synthesis $synthesis
  }
  cd $dir

  foreach cmd $cmd_list {
    puts "Executing cmd: $cmd"
    eval $cmd
  }

  prj_save
  prj_close

  cd $dir
}

###############################################################################
## Adds files to the specified project by searching them in the specyfied
## '-spath' folder '-sdepth' deep.
## You can use with normalized paths, or with paths relative to the Radiant
## project file .rdf for spath (search path).
## The ppath (project path) must be a folder that contains the .rdf project
## file max 3 directory deep.
#
# \opt[exts] -exts {csacsi.v a_szamar.v *.ipx}
# \opt[spath] -spath ./$project_name/$project_name/lib
# \opt[ppath] -ppath ./$project_name
# \opt[sdepth] -sdepth 7
# \opt[opt_args] -opt_args {<opt args for prj_add_source Radiant tcl command>}
###############################################################################
proc adi_project_files_auto {project_name args} {
  puts "\nadi_project_files_auto:\n"

  array set opt [list -exts {*.ipx} \
    -spath ./_bld/$project_name/$project_name/lib \
    -ppath "./_bld/$project_name" \
    -sdepth "6" \
    -opt_args "" \
    {*}$args]

  set exts $opt(-exts)
  set spath $opt(-spath)
  set ppath $opt(-ppath)
  set sdepth $opt(-sdepth)
  set opt_args $opt(-opt_args)

  puts "args:\n"
  puts "Project path: $ppath"
  puts "Extentions: $exts"
  puts "Search path: $spath"
  puts "search depth: $sdepth"
  puts "Optional arguments: $opt_args\n"

  # Searching for the Radiant project file.
  set sbx_lsit [get_file_list $ppath *${project_name}.rdf 3]
  set radiant_project [lindex $sbx_lsit 0]

  # setting the current directory
  set dir [pwd]

  if { [file exists $radiant_project] == 1} {
    set project_dir [string map [list /${project_name}.rdf ""] $radiant_project]
    puts "\n------Adding files to $radiant_project project.------\n"

    # When I open the Radiant project, this tool enters the directory
    # where the Radiant .rdf project file is.
    # So, if we add files with relative path, then the path must be relative
    # to this file.
    prj_open $radiant_project
    cd $dir

    set flist [get_file_list $spath $exts $sdepth]
    if {$flist != ""} {
      puts "\n------List of files to be added:------ \n"
      foreach file $flist {
        puts $file
      }
    } else {
      puts {No files to be added.}
    }
  } else {
    puts "Project does not exist."
    exit 2
  }

  puts "\n"

  foreach pfile $flist {
    puts "Trying to add $pfile to the $radiant_project project"

    # In Lattice Radiant there can be only one active .sdc (Pre-Synthesis
    # Constraint File) and one active .pdc (Post-Synthesis Constraint File).
    # Generating a single system_constr.sdc and a single system_constr.pdc
    # from multiple .sdc and .pdc constraint files.
    if {[regexp {^.+\.pdc$} $pfile]} {
      add_update_constraint_file $pfile $project_dir pdc $radiant_project $opt_args
    } elseif {[regexp {^.+\.sdc$} $pfile]} {
      add_update_constraint_file $pfile $project_dir sdc $radiant_project $opt_args
    } else {
      if { [catch {prj_add_source $opt_args $pfile} fid] } {
        puts "$pfile already added to $radiant_project project!"
      }
    }
  }

  prj_save
  prj_close

  # changing directory back, because Radiant enters the project directory
  # and lets it like that so if we use relative paths somewhere in scripts
  # it would affect our code.
  cd $dir
}

###############################################################################
## Procedure to update parameter values in an existing Verilog file
##
## Usage:
##   update_verilog_parameters \
##     -input_file "system_top.v" \
##     -output_file "system_top_modified.v" \
##     -parameters {ALERT_SPI_N 1 NUM_OF_SDI 4}
##
## Parameters:
##   -input_file: Path to the input Verilog file
##   -output_file: Path to the output file (can be same as input)
##   -parameters: List of parameter name-value pairs {NAME1 VALUE1 NAME2 VALUE2}
###############################################################################
proc update_verilog_parameters {args} {
  array set opt [list -input_file "" \
    -output_file "" \
    -parameters {} \
    {*}$args]

  set input_file $opt(-input_file)
  set output_file $opt(-output_file)
  set parameters $opt(-parameters)

  if {$input_file == ""} {
    puts "ERROR: -input_file is required"
    return -code error
  }

  if {$output_file == ""} {
    set output_file $input_file
  }

  if {![file exists $input_file]} {
    puts "ERROR: Input file '$input_file' does not exist"
    return -code error
  }

  # Build parameter override map
  array set param_map {}
  if {[llength $parameters] % 2 != 0} {
    puts "WARNING: Parameter list has odd length; last entry ignored"
  }
  foreach {pname pval} $parameters {
    set param_map([string trim $pname]) [string trim $pval]
  }

  # Read the input file
  set fid [open $input_file r]
  set data [read $fid]
  close $fid

  # Process line by line and update parameter values
  set lines [split $data "\n"]
  set new_lines {}
  set updated_params {}

  foreach line $lines {
    set updated_line $line
    # Match parameter lines: parameter NAME = VALUE
    if {[regexp {^(\s*parameter\s+)(\w+)(\s*=\s*)([^,;]+)(.*)} $line -> prefix pname eq pval suffix]} {
      set pname [string trim $pname]
      if {[info exists param_map($pname)]} {
        set new_val $param_map($pname)
        set updated_line "${prefix}${pname}${eq}${new_val}${suffix}"
        lappend updated_params $pname
        puts "Updated parameter: $pname = $pval -> $new_val"
      }
    }
    lappend new_lines $updated_line
  }

  # Write output file
  set fout [open $output_file w]
  puts $fout [join $new_lines "\n"]
  close $fout

  puts "\nUpdated file: $output_file"
  if {[llength $updated_params] > 0} {
    puts "Updated parameters: [join $updated_params {, }]"
  } else {
    puts "No parameters were updated"
  }

  # Check for parameters that weren't found
  foreach {pname pval} $parameters {
    set pname [string trim $pname]
    if {[lsearch $updated_params $pname] == -1} {
      puts "WARNING: Parameter '$pname' not found in file"
    }
  }
}

###############################################################################
## Parses a parameter file and returns a parameter list.
## File format: NAME=VALUE (one per line, # for comments)
##
## Usage:
##   set param_list [parse_parameter_file "system_top_parameters.txt"]
##
## Returns:
##   A list in format {NAME1 VALUE1 NAME2 VALUE2 ...}
###############################################################################
proc parse_parameter_file {file_path} {
  if {![file exists $file_path]} {
    puts "WARNING: Parameter file '$file_path' does not exist"
    return {}
  }

  set param_list {}
  set fid [open $file_path r]
  
  while {[gets $fid line] >= 0} {
    # Skip empty lines and comments
    set line [string trim $line]
    if {$line == "" || [string index $line 0] == "#"} {
      continue
    }
    
    # Parse NAME=VALUE format
    if {[regexp {^([^=]+)=(.*)$} $line -> pname pval]} {
      set pname [string trim $pname]
      set pval [string trim $pval]
      lappend param_list $pname $pval
    }
  }
  
  close $fid
  
  if {$param_list != ""} {
    puts "Parsed [expr {[llength $param_list] / 2}] parameters from $file_path"
  }
  
  return $param_list
}

###############################################################################
## Adds files to the specified project.
## The ppath (project path) must be a folder that contains the .rdf project
## file max 3 directory deep.
#
# \opt[ppath] -ppath ./$project_name
# \opt[flist] -flist {./csacsi.v ./a_szamar.v}
# \opt[opt_args] -opt_args {<opt args for prj_add_source Radiant tcl command>}
###############################################################################
proc adi_project_files {project_name args} {
  puts "\nadi_project_files:\n"

  array set opt [list -ppath "./_bld/$project_name" \
    -flist "" \
    -opt_args "" \
    -top_module_file_in "system_top.v" \
    -top_module_file_out "_bld/system_top.v" \
    -top_module_par_list {} \
    -param_file "./_bld/system_top_parameters.txt" \
    {*}$args]

  set ppath $opt(-ppath)
  set flist $opt(-flist)
  set opt_args $opt(-opt_args)
  set top_module_file_in $opt(-top_module_file_in)
  set top_module_file_out $opt(-top_module_file_out)
  set top_module_par_list $opt(-top_module_par_list)
  set param_file $opt(-param_file)

  # Check if parameter file exists and load parameters
  set file_param_list [parse_parameter_file $param_file]
    
  # Merge file parameters with command-line parameters (command-line takes precedence)
  set top_module_par_list [dict merge $file_param_list $top_module_par_list]

  # Generate or update parameter file from merged parameter list
  if {[llength $top_module_par_list] > 0} {
    set fout [open $param_file w]
    puts $fout "# System top parameters"
    puts $fout "# Generated on [clock format [clock seconds]]"
    puts $fout ""
    foreach {pname pval} $top_module_par_list {
      puts $fout "$pname=$pval"
    }
    close $fout
    puts "Generated parameter file: $param_file"
  }

    # Top module parameter injection and file list replacement logic
  if {$top_module_par_list != ""} {
    puts "Top module processing: in='$top_module_file_in' out='$top_module_file_out'"

    # Replace occurrences of input top module file with output file path in flist
    set new_flist {}
    set top_file_found {}
    foreach f $flist {
      if {[file tail $f] eq [file tail $top_module_file_in]} {
        lappend new_flist $top_module_file_out
        set top_file_found $f
        puts "Replacing $f with $top_module_file_out in file list"
      } else {
        lappend new_flist $f
      }
    }
    set flist $new_flist

    if {$top_file_found == ""} {
      puts "WARNING: Top module file '$top_module_file_in' not found in file list"
    } else {
      puts "Updating parameters in top module file '$top_file_found'"
        update_verilog_parameters \
          -input_file $top_file_found \
          -output_file $top_module_file_out \
          -parameters $top_module_par_list
    }
  }

  # Searching for the Radiant project file.
  set sbx_lsit [get_file_list $ppath *${project_name}.rdf 3]
  set radiant_project [lindex $sbx_lsit 0]

  # setting the current directory
  set dir [pwd]

  if { [file exists $radiant_project] == 1} {
    set project_dir [string map [list /${project_name}.rdf ""] $radiant_project]
    puts "\n------Adding files to $radiant_project project.------\n"

    # When I open the Radiant project, this tool enters the directory
    # where the Radiant .rdf project file is.
    # So, if we add files with relative path, then the path must be relative
    # to this file.
    prj_open $radiant_project
    cd $dir

    if {$flist != ""} {
      puts "\n------List of manually defined files to be added:------ \n"
      foreach file $flist {
        puts $file
      }
    } else {
      puts {No manually defined files to be added.}
    }
  } else {
    puts "Project does not exist."
    exit 2
  }

  puts "\n"

  foreach pfile $flist {
    puts "Trying to add $pfile to the $radiant_project project"

    # In Lattice Radiant there can be only one active .sdc (Pre-Synthesis
    # Constraint File) and one active .pdc (Post-Synthesis Constraint File).
    # Generating a single system_constr.sdc and a single system_constr.pdc
    # from multiple .sdc and .pdc constraint files.
    if {[regexp {^.+\.pdc$} $pfile]} {
      add_update_constraint_file $pfile $project_dir pdc $radiant_project $opt_args
    } elseif {[regexp {^.+\.sdc$} $pfile]} {
      add_update_constraint_file $pfile $project_dir sdc $radiant_project $opt_args
    } else {
      if { [catch {prj_add_source $opt_args $pfile} fid] } {
        puts "$pfile already added to $radiant_project project!"
      }
    }
  }

  prj_save
  prj_close

  # changing directory back, because Radiant enters the project directory
  # and lets it like that so if we use relative paths somewhere in scripts
  # it would affect our code.
  cd $dir
}

proc add_update_constraint_file {pfile project_dir ext radiant_project opt_args} {
      puts "Adding $pfile to $project_dir/system_constr.$ext"
      set file [open $pfile]
      set data [read $file]
      close $file

      set file_out [open "$project_dir/system_constr.$ext" a]
      puts $file_out "\n# $pfile\n\n$data"
      close $file_out

      if { [catch {prj_add_source $opt_args $project_dir/system_constr.$ext} fid] } {
        puts "$project_dir/system_constr.$ext already added to $radiant_project project!"
      }
}

# Adds the default project files to the Radiant project ($project_name.rdf)
proc adi_project_files_default {project_name} {
  adi_project_files_auto $project_name -exts {*.ipx} \
    -spath "./_bld/$project_name/$project_name/lib" \
    -ppath "./_bld/$project_name" \
    -sdepth "6"
  adi_project_files $project_name \
    -flist [list ./_bld/$project_name/$project_name/$project_name.v]
}

###############################################################################
## Returns a list of files in a given path searching recursively.
#
# \param[path] - the base directory
# \param[extension_list] - the list of extension files, for example:
#                                                              {*.v *.tcl *.xdc}
# \param[depth] - the depth of recursive search
# \return - file_list
#
# The return path depends on what path you use as input.
# For example you can use like:
#                                    get_file_list [file normalize ./] {*.ipx} 7
#   to get the list of .ipx files from the current directory 7 directories deep
#   with normalized paths or you can use with relative paths like:
#                                                     get_file_list ./ {*.ipx} 7
###############################################################################
proc get_file_list {path {extension_list {*.ipx}} {depth 5}} {
  set file_list {}
  foreach ext $extension_list {
    set file_list [list {*}$file_list \
      {*}[glob -nocomplain -type f -directory $path $ext]]
  }
  if {$depth > 0} {
    foreach dir [glob -nocomplain -type d -directory $path *] {
      set file_list [list {*}$file_list \
        {*}[get_file_list $dir $extension_list [expr {$depth-1}]]]
    }
  }
  return $file_list
}

###############################################################################
## Returns a list of file paths and replaces the base_to_cut part
## at start of file paths with base_to_add.
#
# \param[full_path_flist] - list of file paths
# \param[base_to_cut] - the start of file paths to cut
# \param[base_to_add] - the start of file paths to add
###############################################################################
proc adopt_path {full_path_flist base_to_cut {base_to_add ""}} {
  set bpath_length [string length $base_to_cut]
  set flist {}

  foreach file $full_path_flist {
    set flist [list {*}$flist \
      $base_to_add[string range $file [expr {$bpath_length + 1}] end]]
  }

  return $flist
}

###############################################################################
## Runs the Radiant project with the defined options.
## Optionally runs a list of commands before running the design in specified
## in specified mode.
## Searches for the .rdf project 3 directories deep from -ppath (project path).
#
# \opt[ppath] -ppath ./$project_name
# \opt[mode] -mode synth
# \opt[impl] -impl "impl_1"
# \opt[top] -top "system_top"
# \opt[cmd_list] -cmd_list {{source csacsi.tcl} {source a_szamar.tcl}}
###############################################################################
proc adi_project_run {project_name args} {
  puts "\nadi_project_run:\n"

  array set opt [list -ppath "./_bld/$project_name" \
    -mode "export" \
    -impl "impl_1" \
    -top "system_top" \
    -cmd_list "" \
    {*}$args]

  set ppath $opt(-ppath)
  set mode $opt(-mode)
  set impl $opt(-impl)
  set top $opt(-top)
  set cmd_list $opt(-cmd_list)

  set sbx_lsit [get_file_list $ppath *${project_name}.rdf 3]
  set radiant_project [lindex $sbx_lsit 0]

  set dir [pwd]

  if {[file exists $radiant_project] == 1} {
    prj_open $radiant_project
    cd $dir
  } else {
    puts "\nProject does not exist.\n"
    exit 2
  }

  prj_set_impl_opt -impl $impl "include path" "."
  prj_set_impl_opt -impl $impl "top" $top

  foreach cmd $cmd_list {
    puts "Executing cmd: $cmd"
    eval $cmd
  }

  if {[string match "export" $mode]} {
    puts "\nRun Export design.\n"
    prj_run Export -impl $impl
  } elseif {[string match "synth" $mode]} {
    puts "\nRun Synthesis design.\n"
    prj_run Synthesis -impl $impl
  } elseif {[string match "map" $mode]} {
    puts "\nRun Map design.\n"
    prj_run Map -impl $impl
  } elseif {[string match "par" $mode]} {
    puts "\nRun PAR design.\n"
    prj_run PAR -impl $impl
  } else {
    puts "\nRun Export design.\n"
    prj_run Export -impl $impl
  }

  prj_save
  prj_close

  cd $dir
}

###############################################################################
## Opens the Radiant project and runs a list of commands given as option
## saves and closes the project.
## Searches for the .rdf project 3 directories deep from -ppath (project path).
#
# \opt[ppath] -ppath ./$project_name
# \opt[cmd_list] -cmd_list {{source csacsi.tcl} {source a_szamar.tcl}}
###############################################################################
proc adi_project_run_cmd {project_name args} {
  puts "\nadi_project_run_cmd:\n"
  set dir [pwd]

  array set opt [list -ppath "./_bld/$project_name" -cmd_list "" {*}$args]
  set ppath $opt(-ppath)
  set cmd_list $opt(-cmd_list)

  set sbx_lsit [get_file_list $ppath *${project_name}.rdf 3]
  set radiant_project [lindex $sbx_lsit 0]

  if { [file exists $radiant_project] == 1} {
    prj_open $radiant_project
    cd $dir
  } else {
    puts "\nProject does not exist.\n"
    exit 2
  }

  foreach cmd $cmd_list {
    puts "Executing cmd: $cmd"
    eval $cmd
  }

  prj_save
  prj_close

  cd $dir
}

1	.. _architecture:
2	
3	HDL Architecture
4	===============================================================================
5	
6	Every HDL design of a reference project can be divided into:
7	
8	#. Base design for the **carrier** board (projects/common/$CARRIER) ---
9	   description of what the carrier contains
10	
11	   - an embedded processor - soft or hard;
12	   - all the peripheral IPs (that are necessary to run a Linux distribution
13	     on the system);
14	   - these designs are specific to each carrier, making them **carrier
15	     dependent**;
16	   - it describes part of the ``system_wrapper`` module;
17	   - located in :git-hdl:`projects/common`; one for each carrier;
18	   - here we do most of the PS configuration, add SPI, I2C and GPIOs;
19	   - in some cases, we have scripts to instantiate the PL DDR as ADC offload
20	     memory or DAC offload memory.
21	
22	#. Base design for the **evaluation** board (projects/$EVAL_BOARD/common)
23	   --- description of what the evaluation contains
24	
25	   - instantiates all the necessary IPs to control the evaluation board and to
26	     capture or send data;
27	   - the data paths defined in this block design are common across multiple
28	     carrier platforms, making them **carrier independent**;
29	   - it describes part of the ``system_wrapper`` module;
30	   - located at ``hdl/projects/$EVAL_BOARD/common`` (``*_bd.tcl`` for
31	     AMD Xilinx FPGAs, and ``*_qsys.tcl`` for Intel FPGAs).
32	
33	#. Specific design for the system (projects/$EVAL_BOARD/$CARRIER)
34	
35	   - we source the carrier board configuration (#1), then the evaluation
36	     board configuration (#2) and then we do some specific parameter
37	     modification, if required.
38	
39	How they're instantiated
40	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
41	
42	In case of a project, inside the ``system_bd.tcl`` file we have to source
43	the base design of the carrier first (#1), then the base design of the
44	evaluation board (#2).
45	
46	Example
47	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
48	
49	Take :adi:`FMCOMMS2 <AD-FMCOMMS2-EBZ>` with
50	:xilinx:`ZedBoard <products/boards-and-kits/1-8dyf-11.html>`;
51	the ``system_bd.tcl`` file will have the following designs sourced to be used:
52	
53	.. code-block:: tcl
54	
55	   source $ad_hdl_dir/projects/common/zed/zed_system_bd.tcl
56	   source ../common/fmcomms2_bd.tcl
57	
58	Typical project diagram
59	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
60	
61	.. image:: ./sources/base_platform.svg
62	
63	Base Design
64	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
65	
66	The base design contains all the I/O peripherals, memory interfaces
67	and processing components, which are necessary for a fully functional
68	Linux system. The majority of these components are Intel and AMD Xilinx IP
69	cores.
70	
71	Usually, they contain:
72	
73	- Microprocessor
74	- Memory interface controller
75	- Peripheral interfaces
76	
77	Microprocessor
78	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
79	
80	In our designs, we use only three types:
81	
82	.. list-table::
83	   :header-rows: 2
84	
85	   * - Intel
86	     -
87	     - AMD Xilinx
88	     -
89	     -
90	     - Lattice
91	   * - **SoC**
92	     - **FPGA**
93	     - **SoC**
94	     - **FPGA**
95	     - `ACAP`_
96	     - **FPGA**
97	   * - `HPS`_
98	     - `NIOS II`_
99	     - `PS7`_
100	       `PS8`_
101	     - `MicroBlaze`_
102	     - `Versal`_
103	     - `riscv-rx`_
104	
105	.. _ACAP: https://www.xilinx.com/an/adaptive-compute-acceleration-platforms.html
106	.. _HPS: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/programmable/683458/current/hard-processor-system-hps.html
107	.. _NIOS II: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/programmable/processor/nios-ii.html
108	.. _PS7: https://www.xilinx.com/products/intellectual-property/processing_system7.html
109	.. _PS8: https://www.xilinx.com/products/intellectual-property/zynq-ultra-ps-e.html
110	.. _MicroBlaze: https://www.xilinx.com/products/design-tools/microblaze.html
111	.. _Versal: https://www.xilinx.com/products/silicon-devices/acap/versal.html
112	.. _riscv-rx: https://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftwareandip/intellectualproperty/ipcore/ipcores04/risc-v-rx-cpu
113	
114	Worth mentioning in case of SoCs, the **Hard Processor System** (HPS)
115	or **Processing System 7/8** (PS7/8) do not contain just the dual-core
116	ARM® Cortex® - A9 MPCore™ processor, they also have other integrated
117	peripherals and memory interfaces. For more information please visit
118	the manufacturer's website, listed in the table above.
119	
120	- ``PS7`` --- `Zynq-7000 SoC Processing
121	  System <https://docs.xilinx.com/v/u/en-US/pg082-processing-system7>`__
122	  (``processing_system7``)
123	- ``PS8`` --- `Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC Processing
124	  System <https://docs.xilinx.com/viewer/book-attachment/xFC3qkokxbD~75kj6nPLuw/2o4flzqn5OqWHaMHwpG3Qg>`__
125	  (``zynq_ultra_ps_e``)
126	- ``Versal`` --- `Versal ACAP
127	  CIPS <https://docs.xilinx.com/r/en-US/pg352-cips/Overview>`__
128	  (``versal_cips``)
129	
130	Memory interface controller
131	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
132	
133	In almost all cases, the carrier board is not made and designed by
134	:adi:`Analog Devices <>`, so the external memory solution of the system is
135	given.
136	
137	Meaning, **we cannot support, modify or alter this important part** of the
138	system. In several cases we even have system limitations because of it
139	(e.g. the memory interface is not fast enough to handle the required
140	data throughput).
141	
142	In the following two links, one can find the landing page of the available
143	memory solutions for Intel and AMD:
144	
145	- Intel's memory interfaces:
146	  https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/programmable/support/support-resources/external-memory.html
147	- AMD's memory interfaces:
148	  https://www.xilinx.com/products/intellectual-property/mig.html#documentation
149	
150	Peripheral interfaces
151	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
152	
153	These interfaces are used to control external peripherals located on
154	the prototyping board or the FMC I/O board.
155	
156	In HDL, these ports are named slightly different than how they're in
157	the documentations. Thus, to make it easier for beginners, here you
158	have the naming of the ports depending on the microprocessor used.
159	
160	.. _architecture cpu-intercon-addr:
161	
162	CPU/Memory interconnects addresses
163	^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
164	
165	The memory addresses that will be used by software are based on the HDL
166	addresses of the IP register map, to which an offset is added, depending
167	on the architecture of the used FPGA (see also
168	:git-hdl:`ad_cpu_interconnect procedure <projects/scripts/adi_board.tcl>`;
169	architecture is specified by ``sys_zynq`` variable, for AMD FPGAs).
170	
171	**Zynq-7000 and 7 Series**
172	
173	Because this was the original target, this is the reference
174	address used, the common one, to which depending on the architecture,
175	you add an offset to get to the address space for the peripherals (as they
176	differ from one to the other).
177	
178	**Zynq UltraScale+ MP**
179	
180	If the address is between 0x4000_0000 - 0x4FFF_FFFF then the
181	AXI peripherics will be placed in 0x8000_0000 - 0x8FFF_FFFF range
182	by adding 0x4000_0000 to the address.
183	
184	If the address is between 0x7000_0000 - 0x7FFF_FFFF then the
185	AXI peripherics will be placed in 0x9000_0000 - 0x9FFF_FFFF range
186	by adding 0x2000_0000 to the address.
187	
188	**Versal**
189	
190	If the address is between 0x4400_0000 - 0x4FFF_FFFF then the
191	AXI peripherics will be placed in 0xA400_0000 - 0xAFFF_FFFF range
192	by adding 0x6000_0000 to the address.
193	
194	If the address is between 0x7000_0000 - 0x7FFF_FFFF then the
195	AXI peripherics will be placed in 0xB000_0000 - 0xBFFF_FFFF range
196	by adding 0x4000_0000 to the address.
197	
198	**Intel**
199	
200	Applying to DE10-Nano, C5SoC.
201	
202	The address usually (but not always) starts from 0x0002_0000, or the first
203	available block of a bigger size. In Quartus block design you should be
204	able to determine it.
205	
206	SPI
207	^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
208	
209	In general, the base design of the carrier (#1) has two Serial Peripheral
210	Interfaces (SPIs), which are used as a control interface for FMC/HSMC devices.
211	These SPI interfaces are controlled by the integrated SPI controller of the
212	**Hard Processor System** (HPS) or **Processing System 7/8** (PS7/8) or an
213	Intel or AMD SPI controller core.
214	
215	I2C/I2S/SPDIF
216	^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
217	
218	A couple of carriers require these standard interfaces for different purposes
219	(e.g. a configuration interface for an audio peripheral device).
220	These peripherals do not necessarily have vital roles in the reference
221	design -- it's more like a generic goal to support all the provided
222	peripherals of the carrier board.
223	
224	HDMI
225	^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
226	
227	There is HDMI support for all carriers which are using the :adi:`ADV7511`
228	as HDMI transmitter. The HDMI transmitter core can be found
229	:git-hdl:`here (axi_hdmi_tx) <library/axi_hdmi_tx>`.
230	
231	GPIOs
232	^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
233	
234	The general rule of thumb is to define 64 GPIO pins for the design:
235	
236	- bits [31: 0] always belong to the carrier board;
237	- bits [63:32] will be assigned to switches, buttons and/or LEDs, which
238	  can be found on the FMC board;
239	- bits [95:64] will be used when the FPGA type is Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC.
240	
241	When some of these GPIOs are not used, the input pins should have the
242	output pins driven to them, so that
243	:xilinx:`Vivado <products/design-tools/vivado.html>` will not complain about
244	inputs not being assigned to.
245	
246	Depending on the processor type, add these values to the GPIO number
247	from the HDL project to obtain the final number used in software:
248	
249	- PS7 EMIO offset = **54**
250	- PS8 EMIO offset = **78**
251	- MicroBlaze offset = **no offset**
252	- Versal offset = **-32**
253	
254	Connectivity
255	^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
256	
257	- Ethernet
258	- USB OTG
259	
260	These interface designs are borrowed from the golden reference design
261	of the board.
262	
263	Interrupts
264	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
265	
266	When developing the Linux software parts for an HDL project, the
267	interrupts number to the PS have a different number in the software
268	side.
269	
270	Not a rule, but in our designs we preffer to use firstly the interrupts
271	from 15 and to go down to 0. Be careful when assigning one, because it
272	might be used in the base design of the carrier!

274	Always check which are used (in
275	``/projects/common/$carrier/$carrier_system_bd.tcl``)

547	Memory Specifications
548	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
549	
550	This section documents the on-chip and external memory resources of each
551	supported carrier.
552	
553	.. important::
554	
555	   **This section is a work in progress.**
556	
557	   - Data was pulled from a large number of user guides, device datasheets,
558	     and technical reference manuals. **Mistakes or gaps are possible**.
559	   - Memory configurations **can vary between board revisions** so what is
560	     listed here may not match your specific revision.
561	
562	   Always cross-reference with the official documentation for your board
563	   before making any design decisions based on these numbers.
564	
565	On-Chip Memory
566	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
567	
568	- **BRAM** and **UltraRAM** reside in the programmable logic fabric and are
569	  fully available to HDL designs.
570	- **UltraRAM** (288 Kb blocks) is present only on UltraScale+ and Versal
571	  devices.
572	- Lattice CertusPro-NX provides **EBR** (18 Kb) and **LRAM** (512 Kb) blocks.
573	- Intel Arria 10 / Stratix 10 / Agilex 7 use **M20K** (20 Kb) blocks while
574	  Cyclone V uses **M10K** (10 Kb) blocks.
575	- The **PS/HPS OCM SRAM** is a fixed block inside the processor subsystem
576	  (Zynq-7000, Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC, Versal) shared between the
577	  APU/application processors and PL via the OCM interconnect. Cyclone V
578	  and Agilex 7 HPS include a smaller 64 KB or 256 KB OCRAM used by the
579	  preloader before DDR initialisation.

739	External Memory
740	~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
741	
742	
743	  - **PS-side / HPS-side** memory is connected to the hard processor system
744	    and is the primary DRAM for Linux.
745	  - **PL-side / Fabric-side** memory is connected directly to FPGA fabric
746	    I/O banks and is available for HDL data-path designs.
747	  - On **Versal** devices there is no hard PS/PL split; all DDR interfaces
748	    connect via the Network on Chip (NoC).
749	
750	.. note::
751	
752	   **Bandwidth** figures in the tables below are computed as
753	   ``Rate (MT/s) x (effective data width in bytes)``.
754	   On 72-bit ECC interfaces (64-bit data + 8-bit ECC), only the
755	   64-bit / 8-byte data portion is counted - the ECC byte carries
756	   error-correction overhead, not user payload.
757	   Example: a 72-bit DDR4-2666 interface => 2,666 x 8 = ~21.3 GB/s,
758	   not 2,666 x 9 = ~24.0 GB/s.

.. _architecture:

HDL Architecture
===============================================================================

Every HDL design of a reference project can be divided into:

#. Base design for the **carrier** board (projects/common/$CARRIER) ---
   description of what the carrier contains

   - an embedded processor - soft or hard;
   - all the peripheral IPs (that are necessary to run a Linux distribution
     on the system);
   - these designs are specific to each carrier, making them **carrier
     dependent**;
   - it describes part of the ``system_wrapper`` module;
   - located in :git-hdl:`projects/common`; one for each carrier;
   - here we do most of the PS configuration, add SPI, I2C and GPIOs;
   - in some cases, we have scripts to instantiate the PL DDR as ADC offload
     memory or DAC offload memory.

#. Base design for the **evaluation** board (projects/$EVAL_BOARD/common)
   --- description of what the evaluation contains

   - instantiates all the necessary IPs to control the evaluation board and to
     capture or send data;
   - the data paths defined in this block design are common across multiple
     carrier platforms, making them **carrier independent**;
   - it describes part of the ``system_wrapper`` module;
   - located at ``hdl/projects/$EVAL_BOARD/common`` (``*_bd.tcl`` for
     AMD Xilinx FPGAs, and ``*_qsys.tcl`` for Intel FPGAs).

#. Specific design for the system (projects/$EVAL_BOARD/$CARRIER)

   - we source the carrier board configuration (#1), then the evaluation
     board configuration (#2) and then we do some specific parameter
     modification, if required.

How they're instantiated
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In case of a project, inside the ``system_bd.tcl`` file we have to source
the base design of the carrier first (#1), then the base design of the
evaluation board (#2).

Example
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Take :adi:`FMCOMMS2 <AD-FMCOMMS2-EBZ>` with
:xilinx:`ZedBoard <products/boards-and-kits/1-8dyf-11.html>`;
the ``system_bd.tcl`` file will have the following designs sourced to be used:

.. code-block:: tcl

   source $ad_hdl_dir/projects/common/zed/zed_system_bd.tcl
   source ../common/fmcomms2_bd.tcl

Typical project diagram
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

.. image:: ./sources/base_platform.svg

Base Design
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The base design contains all the I/O peripherals, memory interfaces
and processing components, which are necessary for a fully functional
Linux system. The majority of these components are Intel and AMD Xilinx IP
cores.

Usually, they contain:

- Microprocessor
- Memory interface controller
- Peripheral interfaces

Microprocessor
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

In our designs, we use only three types:

.. list-table::
   :header-rows: 2

   * - Intel
     -
     - AMD Xilinx
     -
     -
     - Lattice
   * - **SoC**
     - **FPGA**
     - **SoC**
     - **FPGA**
     - `ACAP`_
     - **FPGA**
   * - `HPS`_
     - `NIOS II`_
     - `PS7`_
       `PS8`_
     - `MicroBlaze`_
     - `Versal`_
     - `riscv-rx`_

.. _ACAP: https://www.xilinx.com/an/adaptive-compute-acceleration-platforms.html
.. _HPS: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/programmable/683458/current/hard-processor-system-hps.html
.. _NIOS II: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/products/programmable/processor/nios-ii.html
.. _PS7: https://www.xilinx.com/products/intellectual-property/processing_system7.html
.. _PS8: https://www.xilinx.com/products/intellectual-property/zynq-ultra-ps-e.html
.. _MicroBlaze: https://www.xilinx.com/products/design-tools/microblaze.html
.. _Versal: https://www.xilinx.com/products/silicon-devices/acap/versal.html
.. _riscv-rx: https://www.latticesemi.com/products/designsoftwareandip/intellectualproperty/ipcore/ipcores04/risc-v-rx-cpu

Worth mentioning in case of SoCs, the **Hard Processor System** (HPS)
or **Processing System 7/8** (PS7/8) do not contain just the dual-core
ARM® Cortex® - A9 MPCore™ processor, they also have other integrated
peripherals and memory interfaces. For more information please visit
the manufacturer's website, listed in the table above.

- ``PS7`` --- `Zynq-7000 SoC Processing
  System <https://docs.xilinx.com/v/u/en-US/pg082-processing-system7>`__
  (``processing_system7``)
- ``PS8`` --- `Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC Processing
  System <https://docs.xilinx.com/viewer/book-attachment/xFC3qkokxbD~75kj6nPLuw/2o4flzqn5OqWHaMHwpG3Qg>`__
  (``zynq_ultra_ps_e``)
- ``Versal`` --- `Versal ACAP
  CIPS <https://docs.xilinx.com/r/en-US/pg352-cips/Overview>`__
  (``versal_cips``)

Memory interface controller
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

In almost all cases, the carrier board is not made and designed by
:adi:`Analog Devices <>`, so the external memory solution of the system is
given.

Meaning, **we cannot support, modify or alter this important part** of the
system. In several cases we even have system limitations because of it
(e.g. the memory interface is not fast enough to handle the required
data throughput).

In the following two links, one can find the landing page of the available
memory solutions for Intel and AMD:

- Intel's memory interfaces:
  https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/programmable/support/support-resources/external-memory.html
- AMD's memory interfaces:
  https://www.xilinx.com/products/intellectual-property/mig.html#documentation

Peripheral interfaces
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

These interfaces are used to control external peripherals located on
the prototyping board or the FMC I/O board.

In HDL, these ports are named slightly different than how they're in
the documentations. Thus, to make it easier for beginners, here you
have the naming of the ports depending on the microprocessor used.

.. _architecture cpu-intercon-addr:

CPU/Memory interconnects addresses
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

The memory addresses that will be used by software are based on the HDL
addresses of the IP register map, to which an offset is added, depending
on the architecture of the used FPGA (see also
:git-hdl:`ad_cpu_interconnect procedure <projects/scripts/adi_board.tcl>`;
architecture is specified by ``sys_zynq`` variable, for AMD FPGAs).

**Zynq-7000 and 7 Series**

Because this was the original target, this is the reference
address used, the common one, to which depending on the architecture,
you add an offset to get to the address space for the peripherals (as they
differ from one to the other).

**Zynq UltraScale+ MP**

If the address is between 0x4000_0000 - 0x4FFF_FFFF then the
AXI peripherics will be placed in 0x8000_0000 - 0x8FFF_FFFF range
by adding 0x4000_0000 to the address.

If the address is between 0x7000_0000 - 0x7FFF_FFFF then the
AXI peripherics will be placed in 0x9000_0000 - 0x9FFF_FFFF range
by adding 0x2000_0000 to the address.

**Versal**

If the address is between 0x4400_0000 - 0x4FFF_FFFF then the
AXI peripherics will be placed in 0xA400_0000 - 0xAFFF_FFFF range
by adding 0x6000_0000 to the address.

If the address is between 0x7000_0000 - 0x7FFF_FFFF then the
AXI peripherics will be placed in 0xB000_0000 - 0xBFFF_FFFF range
by adding 0x4000_0000 to the address.

**Intel**

Applying to DE10-Nano, C5SoC.

The address usually (but not always) starts from 0x0002_0000, or the first
available block of a bigger size. In Quartus block design you should be
able to determine it.

SPI
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

In general, the base design of the carrier (#1) has two Serial Peripheral
Interfaces (SPIs), which are used as a control interface for FMC/HSMC devices.
These SPI interfaces are controlled by the integrated SPI controller of the
**Hard Processor System** (HPS) or **Processing System 7/8** (PS7/8) or an
Intel or AMD SPI controller core.

I2C/I2S/SPDIF
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

A couple of carriers require these standard interfaces for different purposes
(e.g. a configuration interface for an audio peripheral device).
These peripherals do not necessarily have vital roles in the reference
design -- it's more like a generic goal to support all the provided
peripherals of the carrier board.

HDMI
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

There is HDMI support for all carriers which are using the :adi:`ADV7511`
as HDMI transmitter. The HDMI transmitter core can be found
:git-hdl:`here (axi_hdmi_tx) <library/axi_hdmi_tx>`.

GPIOs
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

The general rule of thumb is to define 64 GPIO pins for the design:

- bits [31: 0] always belong to the carrier board;
- bits [63:32] will be assigned to switches, buttons and/or LEDs, which
  can be found on the FMC board;
- bits [95:64] will be used when the FPGA type is Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC.

When some of these GPIOs are not used, the input pins should have the
output pins driven to them, so that
:xilinx:`Vivado <products/design-tools/vivado.html>` will not complain about
inputs not being assigned to.

Depending on the processor type, add these values to the GPIO number
from the HDL project to obtain the final number used in software:

- PS7 EMIO offset = **54**
- PS8 EMIO offset = **78**
- MicroBlaze offset = **no offset**
- Versal offset = **-32**

Connectivity
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

- Ethernet
- USB OTG

These interface designs are borrowed from the golden reference design
of the board.

Interrupts
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

When developing the Linux software parts for an HDL project, the
interrupts number to the PS have a different number in the software
side.

Not a rule, but in our designs we preffer to use firstly the interrupts
from 15 and to go down to 0. Be careful when assigning one, because it
might be used in the base design of the carrier!

Always check which are used (in
``/projects/common/$carrier/$carrier_system_bd.tcl``)

Memory Specifications
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

This section documents the on-chip and external memory resources of each
supported carrier.

.. important::

   **This section is a work in progress.**

   - Data was pulled from a large number of user guides, device datasheets,
     and technical reference manuals. **Mistakes or gaps are possible**.
   - Memory configurations **can vary between board revisions** so what is
     listed here may not match your specific revision.

   Always cross-reference with the official documentation for your board
   before making any design decisions based on these numbers.

On-Chip Memory
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

- **BRAM** and **UltraRAM** reside in the programmable logic fabric and are
  fully available to HDL designs.
- **UltraRAM** (288 Kb blocks) is present only on UltraScale+ and Versal
  devices.
- Lattice CertusPro-NX provides **EBR** (18 Kb) and **LRAM** (512 Kb) blocks.
- Intel Arria 10 / Stratix 10 / Agilex 7 use **M20K** (20 Kb) blocks while
  Cyclone V uses **M10K** (10 Kb) blocks.
- The **PS/HPS OCM SRAM** is a fixed block inside the processor subsystem
  (Zynq-7000, Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC, Versal) shared between the
  APU/application processors and PL via the OCM interconnect. Cyclone V
  and Agilex 7 HPS include a smaller 64 KB or 256 KB OCRAM used by the
  preloader before DDR initialisation.

External Memory
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


  - **PS-side / HPS-side** memory is connected to the hard processor system
    and is the primary DRAM for Linux.
  - **PL-side / Fabric-side** memory is connected directly to FPGA fabric
    I/O banks and is available for HDL data-path designs.
  - On **Versal** devices there is no hard PS/PL split; all DDR interfaces
    connect via the Network on Chip (NoC).

.. note::

   **Bandwidth** figures in the tables below are computed as
   ``Rate (MT/s) x (effective data width in bytes)``.
   On 72-bit ECC interfaces (64-bit data + 8-bit ECC), only the
   64-bit / 8-byte data portion is counted - the ECC byte carries
   error-correction overhead, not user payload.
   Example: a 72-bit DDR4-2666 interface => 2,666 x 8 = ~21.3 GB/s,
   not 2,666 x 9 = ~24.0 GB/s.

File structure of a project
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

.. tip::

   In ``/projects/common/$carrier_name/`` you can find templates for the
   *system_top.v*, *Makefile*, etc. to help you when creating a new project.

Project files for AMD boards
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

A project for an AMD FPGA board should contain the following files:

- ``Makefile`` --- auto-generated file; contains all the IP
  dependencies needed for the project to be built
- ``system_project.tcl`` --- script that creates the actual Vivado
  project and runs the synthesis/implementation of the design
- ``system_bd.tcl`` --- sources the base design of the carrier first, then the
  base design of the evaluation board, and afterwards it contains all the IP
  instances and connections that must be added on top of the sourced files, to
  complete the design of the project (these are **specific** to the
  combination of this carrier and board)
- ``system_constr.xdc`` --- constraints file of the design; it's the
  connection between the physical pins of the FPGA and the HDL code
  that describes the behavior; here you define the FMC I/O pins,
  board-specific clock signals, timing constraints, etc. The
  constraints specific to the carrier are imported in the
  *system_project.tcl* file
- ``system_top.v`` --- contains everything about the HDL part of the
  project; it instantiates the ``system_wrapper`` module, I/O buffers,
  I/ODDRs, modules that transform signals from LVDS to single-ended,
  etc. The I/O ports of this Verilog module will be connected to actual
  I/O pads of the FPGA.

  - ``system_wrapper`` --- is a tool-generated file and can be found at
    ``<project_name>.srcs/sources_1/bd/system/hdl/system_wrapper.v``

    - the I/O ports of this module are declared in either
      *system_bd.tcl* or in the base design of the evaluation board (#2) file
    - this can be visualized in Vivado at the Block Design section
    - the base design, board design and system_bd.tcl describe this
      module, making the connections between the instantiated IPs

Project files for Intel boards
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

A project for an Intel FPGA board should contain the following files:

- ``Makefile`` --- auto-generated file; contains all the IP
  dependencies needed for the project to be built
- ``system_project.tcl`` --- script that creates the actual Quartus
  project and runs the synthesis/implementation of the design. It also
  contains the I/O definitions for the interfaces between the board and
  the FPGA
- ``system_qsys.tcl`` --- also called **platform designer**; sources the base
  design of the carrier first, then the base design of the evaluation board,
  and afterwards it contains all the IP instances and connections that must
  be added on top of the sourced files, to complete the design of the project
  (these are specific to the combination of this carrier and board)
- ``system_constr.sdc`` --- contains clock definitions and other path
  constraints
- ``system_top.v`` --- contains everything about the HDL part of the
  project; it instantiates the ``system_bd`` module, I/O buffers, specific
  SPI modules, modules that transform signals from LVDS to single-ended,
  etc. The I/O ports of this Verilog module will be connected to actual
  I/O pads of the FPGA

Examples
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Some carriers have a different name for these files, for example A10SoC
has constraints file for both PL side and PS side:

- a10soc_plddr4_assign.tcl --- constraints file for the PL
- a10soc_system_assign.tcl --- constraints file for the PS

Project files for Lattice boards
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

A project for a Lattice FPGA board should contain the following files:

- ``Makefile`` --- auto-generated file; contains all the IP
  dependencies needed for the project to be built
- ``system_project_pb.tcl`` --- used to build the Propel Builder project
  (block design); linked in project-lattice.mk, run by propelbld (Windows),
  propelbldwrap (Linux);
- ``system_project.tcl`` --- used to build the Radiant project; Linked in
  project-lattice.mk, run by pnmainc (Windows), radiantc (Linux);
- ``system_pb.tcl`` --- linker script for the projects, sourced in
  adi_project_pb procedure that is called in system_project_pb.tcl and it is
  defined in adi_project_lattice_pb.tcl; sources the base design of the carrier
  first, then the base design of the evaluation board, and afterwards it
  contains all the IP instances and connections that must be added on top of
  the sourced files, to complete the design of the project (these are specific
  to the combination of this carrier and board)
- ``system_constr.sdc`` --- contains clock definitions and other path constraints
- ``system_constr.pdc`` --- contains clock definitions and other path
  constraints  + physical constraints
- ``system_top.v`` --- contains everything about the HDL part of the
  project; it instantiates the **<project_name>.v** ``system_wrapper`` module,
  I/O buffers, I/ODDRs, modules that transform signals from LVDS to single-ended,
  etc. The I/O ports of this Verilog module will be connected to actual
  I/O pads of the FPGA

####################################################################################
## Copyright (c) 2018 - 2023, 2025 Analog Devices, Inc.
## SPDX short identifier: BSD-1-Clause
####################################################################################

# Assumes this file is in projects/scripts/project-xilinx.mk
HDL_PROJECT_PATH := $(subst scripts/project-xilinx.mk,,$(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST)))
HDL_LIBRARY_PATH := $(HDL_PROJECT_PATH)../library/

include $(HDL_PROJECT_PATH)../quiet.mk

# Parse the config file and convert it to environment variables
PARAMS_REPLACE_LIST := JESD LANE # list of words that should be removed from the parameter names
GEN_SED := '$(foreach name, $(PARAMS_REPLACE_LIST), s/$(name)//g;);s/_//g'
ifdef CFG
    include $(CFG)
    export $(shell sed 's/=.*//' $(CFG) | tr '\n' ' ')
    PARAMS := $(shell cat $(CFG) | tr '\n' ' ')
    DIR_NAME := $(basename $(notdir $(CFG)))
endif

VIVADO := vivado -tempDir .Xil -mode batch -source

# Parse the variables passed to make and convert them to the filename format
ifeq ($(shell expr $(MAKELEVEL) % 2),0)
  CMD_VARIABLES := $(shell echo $(-*-command-variables-*-) | tac -s ' ')
else
  CMD_VARIABLES := $(shell echo $(MAKEOVERRIDES))
endif

ifneq ($(strip $(CMD_VARIABLES)), )
    PARAMS := $(shell echo $(CMD_VARIABLES) | sed -e 's/[=]/_/g')
    GEN_NAME := $(shell echo $(PARAMS) | sed -e $(GEN_SED) | sed -e 's/[ .]/_/g')
    DIR_NAME := $(if $(strip $(DIR_NAME)),$(DIR_NAME)_$(GEN_NAME),$(GEN_NAME))
endif

ifneq ($(strip $(DIR_NAME)), )
    PROJECT_NAME := $(DIR_NAME)/$(PROJECT_NAME)
    $(shell test -d $(DIR_NAME) || mkdir $(DIR_NAME))
    ADI_PROJECT_DIR := $(DIR_NAME)/
    export ADI_PROJECT_DIR
	VIVADO := vivado -tempDir $(DIR_NAME)/.Xil -log $(DIR_NAME)/vivado.log -journal $(DIR_NAME)/vivado.jou -mode batch -source
endif

CLEAN_TARGET := *.cache
CLEAN_TARGET += *.data
CLEAN_TARGET += *.xpr
CLEAN_TARGET += xgui
CLEAN_TARGET +=  gui
CLEAN_TARGET += *.runs
CLEAN_TARGET += *.srcs
CLEAN_TARGET += *.sdk
CLEAN_TARGET += *.hw
CLEAN_TARGET += *.sim
CLEAN_TARGET += *.ip_user_files
CLEAN_TARGET += *.str
CLEAN_TARGET += mem_init_sys.txt
CLEAN_TARGET += *.csv
CLEAN_TARGET += *.hbs
CLEAN_TARGET += *.gen
CLEAN_TARGET += *.xpe
CLEAN_TARGET += *.xsa
CLEAN_TARGET += *.log
CLEAN_TARGET += *.jou
ifneq ($(strip $(DIR_NAME)), )
    CLEAN_TARGET := $(addprefix $(DIR_NAME)/,$(CLEAN_TARGET))
endif
CLEAN_TARGET += .Xil

CLEAN_DIRS := $(dir $(wildcard */*_vivado.log))

# Common dependencies that all projects have
M_DEPS += system_project.tcl
M_DEPS += system_bd.tcl
M_DEPS += $(wildcard system_top*.v)
M_DEPS += $(wildcard system_constr*.xdc) # Not all projects have this file
M_DEPS += $(wildcard system_constr*.tcl) # Not all projects have this file
M_DEPS += $(HDL_PROJECT_PATH)scripts/adi_project_xilinx.tcl
M_DEPS += $(HDL_PROJECT_PATH)../scripts/adi_env.tcl
M_DEPS += $(HDL_PROJECT_PATH)scripts/adi_board.tcl
M_DEPS += $(EXTERNAL_DEPS)

M_DEPS += $(foreach dep,$(LIB_DEPS),$(HDL_LIBRARY_PATH)$(dep)/component.xml)

.PHONY: all lib clean clean-all

all: external_dependencies $(PROJECT_NAME).sdk/system_top.xsa

lib: $(M_DEPS)

clean:
	-rm -f reference.dcp
	$(call clean, \
		$(CLEAN_TARGET), \
		$(HL)$(PROJECT_NAME)$(NC) project)
	-rm -Rf ${DIR_NAME}

clean-all: clean
	@rm -Rf $(CLEAN_DIRS)
	@for lib in $(LIB_DEPS); do \
		$(MAKE) -C $(HDL_LIBRARY_PATH)$${lib} clean; \
	done

external_dependencies: external_dependencies_cleanup $(EXTERNAL_DEPS)

external_dependencies_cleanup:
	rm -f missing_external.log

$(EXTERNAL_DEPS):
	if [ ! -d $@ ]; then \
		echo $@ >> missing_external.log ; \
	fi

MODE ?= "default"

$(PROJECT_NAME).sdk/system_top.xsa: $(M_DEPS)
	@if [ $(MODE) = incr ]; then \
		if [ -f */impl_1/system_top_routed.dcp ]; then \
			echo Found previous run result at `ls */impl_1/system_top_routed.dcp`; \
			cp -u */impl_1/system_top_routed.dcp ./reference.dcp ; \
		fi; \
		if [ -f ./reference.dcp ]; then \
			echo Using reference checkpoint for incremental compilation; \
		fi; \
	else \
		rm -f reference.dcp; \
	fi;
	$(call skip_if_missing, \
		Project, \
		$(PROJECT_NAME), \
		true, \
	rm -rf $(CLEAN_TARGET) ; \
	$(call build, \
		$(VIVADO) system_project.tcl, \
		$(PROJECT_NAME)_vivado.log, \
		$(HL)$(PROJECT_NAME)$(NC) project))

$(HDL_LIBRARY_PATH)%/component.xml: TARGET:=xilinx
FORCE:
$(HDL_LIBRARY_PATH)%/component.xml: FORCE
	flock $(dir $@).lock sh -c " \
	if [ -n \"${REQUIRED_VIVADO_VERSION}\" ]; then \
		$(MAKE) -C $(dir $@) $(TARGET) REQUIRED_VIVADO_VERSION=${REQUIRED_VIVADO_VERSION}; \
	else \
		$(MAKE) -C $(dir $@) $(TARGET); \
	fi"; exit $$?

7	# This file contains the following procedures for Lattice Propel Builder
8	# projects:
9	# * adi_project_pb - Sets the device settings based on project_name or manually
10	#     by options.
11	#               - Calls the adi_project_create_pb procedure
12	#               - Optionally you can add a list of tcl commands to be executed
13	#     in adi_project_create_pb after creating the project.
14	# * adi_project_create_pb - Creates the Propel Builder project itself and
15	#     executes some optional commands that are piped trough adi_project_pb
16	#     procedure.
17	# * adi_ip_instance - Creates a Propel Builder ip config file and adds the
18	#     specified ip to the opened project with that configuration.
19	# * adi_ip_update - Updates a specified ip with new configurations and optional
20	#     new name.
21	###############################################################################
22	
23	###############################################################################
24	## Extracts the device parameters from project name.
25	## Calls the adi_project_create_pb procedure with specified parameters.
26	## There is option to pass the Device parameters manually, and an option
27	## to pass a list of tcl commands to be executed after creating the project in
28	## adi_project_create_pb procedure.
29	#
30	# \opt[dev_select] -dev_select "auto"
31	# \opt[ppath] -ppath .
32	# \opt[device] -device "LFCPNX-100-9LFG672C"
33	# \opt[speed] -speed "9_High-Performance_1.0V"
34	# \opt[board] -board "Certus Pro NX Evaluation Board"
35	# \opt[language] -language "verilog"
36	# \opt[cmd_list] -cmd_list {{source ./system_pb.tcl}}
37	# \opt[psc] -psc "${env(TOOLRTF)}/../../templates/MachXO3D_Template01/MachXO3D_Template01.psc"
38	# \opt[parameter_list] -parameter_list {PARAM1 value1 PARAM2 value2}
39	# \opt[custom_questa_prep_tcl] -custom_questa_prep_tcl ""
40	###############################################################################
41	proc adi_project_pb {project_name args} {
42	  puts "\nadi_project_pb:\n"
43	
44	  global env
45	  global ad_hdl_dir
46	  global ad_project_params
47	  set ::project_name $project_name
48	  set preinst_ip_mod_dir ${env(TOOLRTF)}
49	
50	  set ppath "./_bld"
51	
52	  array set opt [list -dev_select "auto" \
53	    -ppath $ppath \
54	    -device "" \
55	    -board "" \
56	    -speed "" \
57	    -language "verilog" \
58	    -psc "${env(TOOLRTF)}/../../templates/MachXO3D_Template01/MachXO3D_Template01.psc" \
59	    -cmd_list {{source ./system_pb.tcl}} \
60	    -interface_paths "$ad_hdl_dir/library/interfaces_ltt/ltt" \
61	    -interface_folder_names {interfaces_ltt} \
62	    -parameter_list {} \
63	    -parameter_file_radiant "$ppath/system_top_parameters.txt" \
64	    -sim_prj_tcl "./system_v_pb.tcl" \
65	    -custom_questa_prep_tcl "" \
66	    {*}$args]
67	
68	  set dev_select $opt(-dev_select)
69	  set ppath [file normalize $opt(-ppath)]
70	  set language $opt(-language)
71	  set cmd_list $opt(-cmd_list)
72	  set psc $opt(-psc)
73	  set interface_paths $opt(-interface_paths)
74	  set interface_folder_names $opt(-interface_folder_names)
75	  set parameter_list $opt(-parameter_list)
76	  set parameter_file_radiant $opt(-parameter_file_radiant)
77	  set sim_prj_tcl $opt(-sim_prj_tcl)
78	  set custom_questa_prep_tcl $opt(-custom_questa_prep_tcl)
79	
80	  # Make parameters available globally for system_pb.tcl
81	  foreach {param value} $parameter_list {
82	    set ad_project_params($param) $value
83	    puts "Setting parameter: $param = $value"
84	  }
85	
86	  if {[file exists $ppath] != 1} {
87	    file mkdir $ppath
88	  }
89	
90	  # Generate system_top_parameters.txt file from parameter_list
91	  if {[llength $parameter_list] > 0} {
92	    set param_file_path "$parameter_file_radiant"
93	    set fout [open $param_file_path w]
94	    puts $fout "# System top parameters"
95	    puts $fout "# Generated on [clock format [clock seconds]]"
96	    puts $fout ""
97	    foreach {pname pval} $parameter_list {
98	      puts $fout "$pname=$pval"
99	    }
100	    close $fout
101	    puts "Generated parameter file: $param_file_path"
102	  }
103	
104	  if { [string match "auto" $dev_select] } {
105	    source $ad_hdl_dir/projects/scripts/adi_lattice_dev_select.tcl
106	  } elseif { [string match "manual" $dev_select] } {
107	    set device $opt(-device)
108	    set board $opt(-board)
109	    set speed $opt(-speed)
110	  }
111	
112	  set interface_paths [lmap path $interface_paths {file normalize $path}]
113	  set interface_paths_found [get_norm_dirs_by_name $ad_hdl_dir/library $interface_folder_names 8]
114	  set interface_paths_found [lmap path $interface_paths_found {list "$path/ltt"}]
115	
116	  set interface_paths [lsort -unique [list {*}$interface_paths {*}$interface_paths_found]]
117	
118	  puts "Interface paths found: $interface_paths_found"
119	  puts "Interface paths used: $interface_paths"
120	
121	  adi_project_create_pb $project_name \
122	    -ppath $ppath \
123	    -device $device \
124	    -board $board \
125	    -speed $speed \
126	    -language $language \
127	    -psc $psc \
128	    -cmd_list $cmd_list \
129	    -parameter_list $parameter_list \

134	###############################################################################
135	## Creates a Propel Builder project with specified parameters.
136	## There is an option to run a list of tcl commands given as parameter after
137	## creating the Propel Builder design.
138	#
139	# \opt[ppath] -ppath .
140	# \opt[device] -device "LFCPNX-100-9LFG672C"
141	# \opt[speed] -speed "9_High-Performance_1.0V"
142	# \opt[board] -board "Certus Pro NX Evaluation Board"
143	# \opt[language] -language "verilog"
144	# \opt[cmd_list] -cmd_list {{source ./system_pb.tcl}}
145	# \opt[custom_questa_prep_tcl] -custom_questa_prep_tcl ""
146	###############################################################################
147	proc adi_project_create_pb {project_name args} {
148	  puts "\nadi_project_create_pb:\n"
149	
150	  global ad_hdl_dir
151	  global ad_project_params
152	  global required_lattice_version
153	  global IGNORE_VERSION_CHECK
154	  global env
155	
156	  array set opt [list -ppath "./_bld" \
157	    -device "" \
158	    -board "" \
159	    -speed "" \
160	    -language "verilog" \
161	    -psc "" \
162	    -cmd_list "" \
163	    -interface_paths "$ad_hdl_dir/library/interfaces_ltt/ltt" \
164	    -sim_prj_tcl "./system_v_pb.tcl" \
165	    -custom_questa_prep_tcl "" \
166	    {*}$args]
167	
168	  set ppath [file normalize $opt(-ppath)]
169	  set device $opt(-device)
170	  set board $opt(-board)
171	  set speed $opt(-speed)
172	  set language $opt(-language)
173	  set psc $opt(-psc)
174	  set cmd_list $opt(-cmd_list)
175	  set interface_paths $opt(-interface_paths)
176	  set sim_prj_tcl $opt(-sim_prj_tcl)
177	  set custom_questa_prep_tcl $opt(-custom_questa_prep_tcl)
178	
179	  # Extracting the Propel Builder version from $env(TOOLRTF)/../../components.xml
180	  set regex "<Name>com\.latticesemi\.systembuilder.*<Version>$required_lattice_version"
181	  set file [open "$env(TOOLRTF)/../../components.xml"]
182	  set data [read $file]
183	  close $file
184	
185	  if {[regexp $regex $data match]} {
186	      regexp <Version>$required_lattice_version $match data
187	      set version [lindex [split $data ">"] 1]
188	      set PROPEL_BUILDER_VERSION $version
189	      puts "Propel Builder version: $PROPEL_BUILDER_VERSION\n"

650	proc get_file_list {path {extension_list {*.v}} {depth 0}} {
651	    set file_list {}
652	    foreach ext $extension_list {
653	        set file_list [list {*}$file_list \
654	        {*}[glob -nocomplain -type f -directory $path $ext]]
655	    }
656	    if {$depth > 0} {
657	        foreach dir [glob -nocomplain -type d -directory $path *] {
658	        set file_list [list {*}$file_list \
659	            {*}[get_file_list $dir $extension_list [expr {$depth-1}]]]
660	        }
661	    }
662	    return $file_list
663	}

695	proc get_lattice_vlnv {xml} {
696	  set regex ".*<lsccip:ip.*>.*<lsccip:general>.*<lsccip:vendor>(.+)</lsccip:vendor>.*<lsccip:library>(.+)</lsccip:library>.*<lsccip:name>(.+)</lsccip:name>.*<lsccip:version>(.+)</lsccip:version>.*</lsccip:general>"
697	  set file [open $xml]
698	  set data [read $file]
699	  close $file
700	  if {[regexp $regex $data -> vnd lib nm vrs]} {
701	    return $vnd:$lib:$nm:$vrs
702	  } else {
703	    return {}
704	  }

709	## Uses get_dir_list to search for each folder name up to 8 folder depths in
710	## default.
711	## Returns a list of unique normalized folder paths.
712	##
713	# \param search_path - The base path to search in

719	proc get_norm_dirs_by_name {search_path {folder_list {interfaces_ltt}} {depth 8}} {
720	  set found_folders {}
